title: Context API and Global State Management
description: Understand how to manage global state in React Native apps using Context API, enabling components to share data without prop drilling.

lessons.title: What is State Management?
lessons.content: State management means handling the data that controls your app’s UI and behavior. In React Native, local state is tied to a component, but sometimes you need to share state across many components—this is where global state management helps.

lessons.title: Problems with Prop Drilling
lessons.content: Prop drilling is passing data through multiple component levels even if intermediate components don't need it. This makes code messy and hard to maintain.

lessons.title: Introducing React’s Context API
lessons.content: Context API allows you to create a global data store accessible by any component, without passing props manually at every level.

When to Use Context API
lessons.content: Context API is great for data that many components need, like user authentication, theme settings, or language preferences. Avoid overusing it for very frequent updates or deeply nested data.

lessons.title: Alternatives to Context API
lessons.content: For complex state management, consider libraries like Redux or MobX. They provide more powerful tools but require more setup.

lessons.title: Summary and Best Practices
lessons.content:
- Use Context API to avoid prop drilling
- Keep context focused on related data
- Avoid updating context too frequently
- Combine Context with local component state
- Always provide default values to avoid errors
